Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the second innings! The umpires are punctual and so are the players of Bangladesh who spread out to the field. Out walk the two openers for India. It's a brand-new opening pair of Sanju Samson and Abhishek Sharma. With the former taking the strike. Shoriful Islam with a slip in place is all in readiness to get the proceedings underway with the new ball. And, here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Well then, the first inning has flown by in this series opener. India has a target within reach to chase and will aim to mirror their bowling performance with the bat as well. Bangladesh on the other hand, will be required to bring their A-game with the ball. They do pose a threatening pace attack and would like them to contribute effectively. An exciting run chase up next in just a few minutes. Stay tuned.

Since the ball did some mischief too, Varun Chakravarthy came in handy and chipped in with a three-wicket haul to his name as well. India didn't let the opposition off the hook in the mid-overs, with identical bowling in the death as well, conceding only 16 runs and taking 3 wickets in the last 4. In the end, Hardik and Arshdeep did the cleaning of the tail effectively, eventually bowling them out in 19.5 overs.

India, on the other hand, began right on the money with Arshdeep setting the foundation in the very first over with a wicket. The new ball moved and got a bit of a variable bounce which helped the seamers to tie the batters up. It was Mayank Yadav though, who created impact straightaway in his debut match. First, delivered a maiden and then snagged his first T20I wicket, adding more trouble to the opposition.

Throughout, Bangladesh looked in a bit of hurry from the word go to accelerate and put the hosts under pressure, but it proved to be a two-faced sword for them. They needed a strong partnership after that initial collapse. But in contrast, they kept losing wickets and slipped down to 111/7 at the end of the 16th over. With an aim to ascend in the death overs, and Mehidy Hasan settled in well by then, he too, was left stranded at one end. As a result, Bangladesh, under steeping pressure, couldn't get the required momentum. Mehidy Hasan though, played well for his unbeaten 35.

Bangladesh started in a bit of a rusty fashion and lost their openers inside the restrictions. The batters tried to adapt to the pitch and tried to take the attack on right away. Hence, they could only mount 39/2 on the board in the Powerplay. In a desperate need to construct partnerships, Najmul Hossain Shanto attempted to launch a counter-offensive. He was the only one who looked settled but searched for partners at the other end.

A comprehensive bowling display by the Men in Blue through and through! They have reduced Bangladesh to just above a run-a-ball in this first T20I. To be fair, the tourists just couldn't get going in the innings and only Najmul Hossain Shanto along with Mehidy Hasan could cross the 20-run mark.

He needs a responsible hand to get Bangladesh to a challenging total. India on the other hand, have not stepped on any wrong foot so far and have continued to chip in with wickets, using the conditions nicely, and will aim to press on further. Gets into a very awkward position and mistimes it badly towards long on where Hardik Pandya takes a safe catch. Hridoy goes back after a struggling 12 off 18. Bangladesh three down now!
Commentary.Howout: c Hardik Pandya b Varun Chakaravarthy
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.4: Varun Chakaravarthy to Towhid Hridoy, OUT! c Hardik Pandya b Varun Chakaravarthy.

Commentary.Commentary: Close! Flatter delivery, short and just around off, skids through, Towhid Hridoy looks to cut it away but this is too close to his body. He misses.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.3: Varun Chakaravarthy to Towhid Hridoy, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: A run after 7 balls! Tossed up, full and around middle, Najmul Hossain Shanto goes down again and sweeps it towards deep square leg for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.2: Varun Chakaravarthy to Najmul Hossain Shanto, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Floated, full and on middle and leg, Najmul Hossain Shanto goes down and paddles it towards short fine. He wants the single but is sent back.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.1: Varun Chakaravarthy to Najmul Hossain Shanto, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Breathless over by Mayank on his debut! No change, Varun Chakaravarthy to continue.

An exceptional first over from Mayank Yadav in T20Is! He pitches it up, on middle, shaping in sharply, Towhid Hridoy only manages to turn it to the leg side. MAIDEN OVER! End of the Powerplay, Bangladesh are 39/2.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.6: Mayank Yadav to Towhid Hridoy, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Make that five dots! Short of a length and outside off, there to be put away, Towhid Hridoy mistimes his cut straight towards cover-point. Pressure building!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.5: Mayank Yadav to Towhid Hridoy, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Four dots in a row now! Back of a length and on off, Towhid Hridoy stays back and dabs it towards backward point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.4: Mayank Yadav to Towhid Hridoy, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Play and a miss! Hits the length hard and around middle, this one skids through, Towhid Hridoy backs away and uses his feet to create room, slashes but gets beaten by the pace.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.3: Mayank Yadav to Towhid Hridoy, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: 145.7 clicks now! Fuller and on middle, angling in, Towhid Hridoy knocks it towards mid off.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.2: Mayank Yadav to Towhid Hridoy, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Good start for the debutant! Mayank Yadav starts with a good-length delivery at 141.8 clicks, outside off, Towhid Hridoy leaves it alone.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.1: Mayank Yadav to Towhid Hridoy, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! Innovative and effective! The Bangladeshi skipper trying to launch a counter-offensive! Much fuller, just a juicy half-volley on the stumps by Varun, Najmul Hossain Shanto reads the line and length early, sits down on his knee and reverse sweeps it over deep point for a six. The ball lands just on the advertising cushions and 15 runs come off Varun Chakaravarthy's first over.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.6: Varun Chakaravarthy to Najmul Hossain Shanto, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: Beaten! Totally missed the line there! Varun Chakaravarthy bowls a loopy one, just outside off, Shanto does not pick the ball off Chakravarthy's fingers, but pokes at it and plays away from the body, gets beaten on the outside edge.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.5: Varun Chakaravarthy to Najmul Hossain Shanto, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: On a length, in front of the pegs, this is worked towards the deep square leg region and this time, Nitish Kumar Reddy is quick enough to intercept the ball. Just a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.4: Varun Chakaravarthy to Towhid Hridoy, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Quality shot that! Short in length, on the stumps, turning in, Towhid Hridoy rocks back and slaps it hard to deep square leg for a cracking boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.3: Varun Chakaravarthy to Towhid Hridoy, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: DROPPED, MISJUDGED, AND FOUR! Full, on off, Towhid Hridoy sits down and slogs it flat towards deep square leg in the air. Nitish Kumar Reddy stationed there overruns to take the catch and lets it through for a boundary. The replay then shows Nitish Kumar Reddy signaling as if the floodlights got in the way and he lost the ball.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.2: Varun Chakaravarthy to Towhid Hridoy, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Varun Chakaravarthy starts his spell. On length, turning in, on middle, Towhid Hridoy tucks it to the strip with soft hands.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.1: Varun Chakaravarthy to Towhid Hridoy, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Hard length again, outside off, Towhid Hridoy cuts it square to deep backward point for a single to end the over.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.6: Hardik Pandya to Towhid Hridoy, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Short of a length wide outisde off. Hridoy charges down but leaves it alone.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: Hardik Pandya to Towhid Hridoy, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Excellent save there by Samson! Angling on the pads, on a short length, Najmul Hossain Shanto misses to pull it away and the ball hits the thigh pad on the way. Deflects and Sanju Samson dives in the direction of the ball to his right. Attempts to stop it with one hand. Gets his glove too, but the ball rolls behind, allowing a leg bye.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Hardik Pandya to Najmul Hossain Shanto, Leg bye.

Commentary.Commentary: Pandya steams in from over the stumps, hurls it full, outside off, Towhid Hridoy bends low and cuts it to point for a quick single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Hardik Pandya to Towhid Hridoy, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Short of a good length, this is tucked away by Shanto to deep square leg for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Hardik Pandya to Najmul Hossain Shanto, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! SHOT! Half-tracker outside off, Najmul Hossain Shanto prepares himself on the back foot and pulls it through mid-wicket for a boundary. He got this from the lower half of the bat and wasn't too far from the mid-wicket fielder.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Hardik Pandya to Najmul Hossain Shanto, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Change? No, Hardik Pandya to continue here.
Hurled full, outside off, Towhid Hridoy lets it through to end the 3rd over. A good positive start for India so far.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Arshdeep Singh to Towhid Hridoy, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Outside off on a length, guided away to point by Hridoy.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Arshdeep Singh to Towhid Hridoy, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Singh delivers a slower one, it is a low full toss on the stumps, Najmul Hossain Shanto tucks it to short mid-wicket. Rinku Singh half-stops it but cannot prevent the single. Looks like he has got a sting on his leg. But good to continue for now.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Arshdeep Singh to Najmul Hossain Shanto, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Steep bumper by Arshdeep this time, attacking the bodyline of the batter. Najmul Hossain Shanto can only sway away from the line. Lets it pass.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Arshdeep Singh to Najmul Hossain Shanto, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Skids through on a good length, outside off, Towhid Hridoy gets ahead on the front foot and taps it through point for a single to get off the mark.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Arshdeep Singh to Towhid Hridoy, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Towhid Hridoy comes out to the middle now.

OUT! PLAYED ON! Inside edge and back into the stumps! Arshdeep Singh gets his second wicket and is all pumped up! Arshdeep Singh lands it outside off on the back of a length, that stays just a tad bit low on the bounce. Seeing the width on offer, Parvez Hossain Emon covers the pegs and goes for a slash with the horizontal bat angle. But, he tries to hit it too hard at it and ends up getting a very healthy inside edge that crashes into the stumps. Both openers for Bangladesh are back in the sheds now within the restrictions.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Arshdeep Singh to Parvez Hossain Emon, OUT! b Arshdeep Singh.

Commentary.Commentary: Quick legs there! A low full toss on off, Parvez Hossain Emon pushes it in front of mid off and charges for a single. Sprints hard and completes it.

Commentary.Commentary: Swing and a miss! Across off on a good length, with a bit of an extra bounce, Parvez Hossain Emon tries to cut it square off the back foot but it is too close to execute that shot. Misses.

Commentary.Commentary: Hardik hits the deck hard, over the top of middle and off, Parvez Hossain Emon taps it to point.

Commentary.Commentary: Surprise bumper by Hardik, on the leg stump line, Parvez Hossain Emon ducks underneath. First bounce called by the umpire.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Hardik Pandya to Parvez Hossain Emon, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! CLUNK! And here comes the first six of the match! Bit too full from Hardik this time, but the line is same on the leg stump, Parvez Hossain Emon picks it up nicely and flicks it up and over deep backward square leg for a six.

Commentary.Commentary: Length delivery to start with by Hardik, on middle and leg, Najmul Hossain Shanto gets on his toes and glances it through square leg for a single.

Commentary.Commentary: Hardik Pandya to share the attack.
Full and shaping outside off. Shanto gets ahead and drives it to wide of mid off for a quick single. End of the first over, Bangladesh are 6/1.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Arshdeep Singh to Najmul Hossain Shanto, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Najmul Hossain Shanto walks out to bat at number 3.

OUT! IN THE AIR AND TAKEN! Arshdeep Singh draws the first blood and it's a pretty good catch by Rinku Singh! Gwalior roars in appreciation as India gets the first breakthrough! Arshdeep Singh bowls a fuller one that tails in, on middle, Litton Das looks to attack him and ends up hitting it across a bit too hard and loses his shape and is also early in his shot. Ends up in an ugly hoick and the ball skies up off the toe end of the bat. It swirls up in the night sky for an eternity over the cover region. Several players converge in to catch it, but Rinku Singh calls for his catch, settles under the skier and takes a sharp catch. Early blow for Bangladesh!
Commentary.Howout: c Rinku Singh b Arshdeep Singh
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Arshdeep Singh to Litton Das, OUT! c Rinku Singh b Arshdeep Singh.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Nicely played by Das! He gets off the mark in style! Length-delivery around off, Litton Das brings his front foot into play, waits for the ball to arrive at him, opens the bat face and guides it past short third for the first boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Arshdeep Singh to Litton Das, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: First runs for Bangladesh and Emon! Much closer to the off pole, with a hint of an away movement, Parvez Hossain Emon covers his stumps and drives it to mid on off the inner half of the bat. Hardik Pandya at mid on runs to his left and gets a bad bounce. Fumbles on the pick-up and parries the ball to the right and allows a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Arshdeep Singh to Parvez Hossain Emon, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Bowls it on an identical length, with the ball shaping away, outside off, Parvez Hossain Emon walks forward and slices it to point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Arshdeep Singh to Parvez Hossain Emon, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Arshdeep charges in with a slip in place, and lands it on the money! Gets a good bit of shape on off, on a good length, Parvez Hossain Emon plays it on the up and drives it straight to the mid off fielder.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Arshdeep Singh to Parvez Hossain Emon, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: All in readiness now! It is a full house in Gwalior and the fans are eagerly waiting for the action to get underway. We can see the Indian team in a huddle and then they spread out to take their respective field positions. Parvez Hossain Emon and Litton Das are the two openers for Bangladesh. Arshdeep Singh has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...

We are moments away from the start of the game but before that, the players from both sides stride out to the middle and line up for their respective national anthems. It will be Bangladesh's first followed by the national anthem of India.

India (Playing XI) - Sanju Samson (WK), Abhishek Sharma, Suryakumar Yadav (C), Nitish Kumar Reddy (On Debut), Hardik Pandya, Riyan Parag, Rinku Singh, Washington Sundar, Varun Chakaravarthy, Arshdeep Singh, Mayank Yadav (On Debut).

Bangladesh (Playing XI) - Najmul Hossain Shanto (C), Litton Das (WK), Parvez Hossain Emon, Towhid Hridoy, Jaker Ali, Mehidy Hasan, Rishad Hossain, Mahmudullah, Taskin Ahmed, Mustafizur Rahman, Shoriful Islam.

Najmul Hossain Shanto, the captain of Bangladesh says it is a pretty new side and a couple of new guys are coming in as well. He is hopeful that they will do something remarkable in this series. Says they have worked really hard for this series. On the pitch, he says he would have bowled first as well but also hopes for the openers to do good. Informs they are going with three seamers and two regular spinners along with six proper batters.

Suryakumar Yadav, the captain of India says that it is a bit humid and does not think it will change much during the game. Adds that it is always nice to play in front of home fans and in home conditions. Mentions that there is a lot of talent in the group and everyone is ready to get on. Tells that the wicket looks good and the crowd has come in numbers as well which is nice to see. Ends by saying that choosing an XI from such a great squad is a nice headache to have and the players who are playing deserve this opportunity. Informs that the players who miss out are Tilak Verma, Harshit Rana, Jitesh Sharma and Ravi Bishnoi.
TOSS UPDATE - Energetic Ravi Shastri hosts the toss! The flip of the coin lands in the favor of India and Suryakumar Yadav elects to BOWL first.

PITCH REPORT - Abhinav Mukund is at the 22 yards inspecting the deck. He begins by sharing the dimensions of this brand new stadium. Mentions it is 64 meters and 65 meters at the squares, and 74 meter hit down the ground. Adds it looks like a typical Indian wicket and is a black soil surface laid with grass on top. Also tells the grass looks quite dry and the pitch is firm as well. Also says that the curator spoke to him and said that the there's been no dew at all since the last few days. Ends by saying it would be a brave decision to bat considering it is a fresh surface.

JUST IN - Pace sensation Mayank Yadav has been handed over the debut cap by Murali Kartik. He was seen marking his run-up a few minutes back. He will make his T20I debut in this match alongside an impressive all-rounder, Nitish Kumar Reddy who was handed the cap by Parthiv Patel.

India has historically dominated their T20I encounters with Bangladesh, boasting an impressive 12-1 win-loss record. Bangladesh's lone victory against India in this format came back in 2019 in New Delhi. Since then, India has maintained its upper hand and has run through this opposition. Will Bangladesh hit a surprise this time around, or will India further better their home record? Only time will tell. With all said, it’s time for the toss and team updates in a bit. Stick around!

Bangladesh, on the other hand, will be led by Najmul Hossain Shanto. They have fielded a comparatively experienced squad with several players having more than fifty T20Is under their belt. But, it would be interesting to see who fills in the shoes of Shakib Al Hasan as the mainstream all-rounder. They do have Mehidy Hasan Miraz for these honors. While the team relies largely on its veteran core, eyes will be on emerging talents like Rishad Hossain and Tanzim Hasan Sakib, who are set to play crucial roles in the bowling department.

India will be missing established openers like Jaiswal and Gill, but the team sees an opportunity for in-form Abhishek Sharma up top. Sanju Samson, who has been a hit-and-miss so far, is also itching to make his mark. The middle order, anchored by Rinku Singh and Riyan Parag with support from Hardik Pandya, aims to provide stability. Tilak Varma's inclusion, following Shivam Dube's injury, adds depth to the batting lineup. In the bowling department, Arshdeep Singh leads the pace attack, and is joined by promising newcomers Harshit Rana and the fiery speedster Mayank Yadav. The spin trio of Bishnoi, Chakravarthy, and Sundar rounds out a diverse bowling unit.

India enters this series with a revamped lineup, helmed by the dynamic Suryakumar Yadav. The team aims to build on its recent successes against Sri Lanka and Zimbabwe earlier this year, and it navigates a transitional phase following the exits of stalwarts like Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli, and Ravindra Jadeja from this format. In contrast, Bangladesh returns to T20I cricket for the first time since the T20 World Cup a few months back. After a streak of lackadaisical performances, Bangladesh is eager to turn things around and prove their mettle this time around.

On that note, we welcome you all joining us for our coverage of this 1st T20I. It’s a debut, not for a player, but for a venue long waiting for this day. The brand new Shrimant Madhavrao Scindia Cricket Stadium of Gwalior will host its first-ever international cricket match. While Gwalior itself is no stranger to hosting cricket, having previously hosted iconic matches at the old Captain Roop Singh Stadium, this is a historic debut for this particular venue to carry forward the legacy.

A T20I series sandwiched between a stacked-up Test season is another treat for the fans as India hosts Bangladesh for a riveting 3-match T20I series. After a successful Test series win by 2-0, India strides out with fresh energy with a re-engineered squad. While Bangladesh on the other hand will be aiming for a stronger performance this time around and challenge the hosts.
... MATCH DAY ...

After securing a dominant 2-0 clean sweep in the Test series, India is now geared up to host Bangladesh in an exciting 3-match T20I series. The opener will be held at the newly inaugurated Shrimant Madhavrao Scindia Cricket Stadium in Gwalior, marking the much-anticipated return of international cricket to the city after 14 long years. The intensity is expected to soar as Bangladesh looks to bounce back from their Test defeats, aiming for a more clinical performance in the shorter format, where they are known to be more formidable. Meanwhile, India, featuring a rejuvenated lineup, will aim to extend their dominance and begin shaping the future of the team as they transition from the era of a few recently retired veterans. Bangladesh brings a formidable squad into this series, not only well-rounded but packed with genuine match-winners. Their experienced batting lineup will be key, carrying the weight of expectations as they look to set the tone. The return of Mehidy Hasan into the squad is a significant boost, adding balance and depth to the squad. Spin will undoubtedly be a crucial factor, but the pacers, led by Mustafizur Rahman, will also have to step up to provide the necessary support in what promises to be a tightly contested series. On the other hand, India enters the series with a few notable players rested, creating opportunities for emerging talent to make an impact. With Abhishek Sharma as the only designated opener, Sanju Samson might partner him at the top. While the middle order appears solid, all eyes will be on the pace department, where speedster Mayank Yadav along with Harshit Rana could make their debut in this series, eager to leave their mark. Both teams look strong on paper and have the capability to outplay each other on any given day. The opener is perfectly set to be a high-intensity contest, as both India and Bangladesh will be eager to seize an early advantage. Who do you think will land the first blow? We'll soon find out!
